Sources: verification/catalogue/pages/http.md (its sources: list is the backbone), verification/library/vox_http.md, research/mastery-20260927/runtime-checks-testing.md section 8 (total classifiers with error values), verification/catalogue/pages/_trust.md (shared base, Vox_sequence.length), and the code at HEAD (8479634adc).
title: Incremental HTTP request parser
summary: `Vox_http` parses HTTP/1.1 requests from input delivered in chunks. Every function in its interface is total, and bad input is a value: the parser's status is `Incomplete`, `Complete request`, `Malformed reason` or `Limit resource`, and the specification's own `framing` classifies header lines the same way. The laws prove soundness and completeness against a request grammar, exact byte accounting, and that the split into chunks does not matter.
The [catalogue page](demo:http) states the claim, the supported subset and the scope.

stops.title: The specification: well_formed and framing
stops.text: `well_formed` defines the requests the parser must complete: a valid request line, header lines that contain no CR or LF and each pass `valid_header`, headers that `framing` accepts with a body of exactly the framed length, and a serialization of at most 16,384 bytes. `framing`, above it, is itself a total classifier over header lines: it returns `Length n`, `Bad e` for a malformed request or `Too_large r` for a resource limit, and rejects every Transfer-Encoding. `framing` uses the named predicates `has_transfer_encoding` and `has_content_length`; their byte-list definitions appear above it. Every definition is `[@def]`, and [`vox_http_spec.mli`](src:verification/library/vox_http_spec.mli) restates each one as a checked equation (`well_formed_def` and so on) for clients that see only the interface.

stops.title: The pure incremental semantics
stops.text: The semantic state contains the partial line, headers and body in wire order, the phase, the pending-CR flag and the remaining budget. `finish_line` uses the public grammar and framing definitions; `step` specifies byte and CRLF errors and body completion. `feed` stops at a terminal state, consumes nothing from an empty chunk, and returns the next byte untouched when an incomplete state has exhausted its budget. `status` and `core_wire` define all parser observations. These are pure definitions; reachability and the reversed-list simulation remain in `vox_http.ml`.

stops.title: An abstract state and total observations
stops.text: A parser state is abstract. Its erased `model` observation exposes the forward-order semantic state. `initial` fixes that state to `Model.initial ()`; the ordinary observations let a client inspect parsing status and byte counts.

stops.title: What one call of feed guarantees
stops.from: (** Feed one chunk according to the pure incremental model.
stops.text: `feed` returns the next state and untouched suffix prescribed by `Model.feed`. `parse` starts at `initial ()` and states soundness directly: a completed request is well formed and its serialization followed by the returned suffix reconstructs the input. Derived observation and chunking laws follow these operations in the full interface.

stops.title: A client proof, and validation of untrusted bytes
stops.text: `decode_serialized` proves completeness for one request: parsing `serialize request` followed by any suffix completes with that request and returns the suffix. The fact comes from the law `roundtrip`, called under `ghost_` and erased. `accept_untrusted` is the idiom for untrusted input: a total parse and a match on the status, where the `Complete` branch gets, from `body_agreement`, that the request is `well_formed`, has no Transfer-Encoding, and has a body whose length every Content-Length states. The error statuses pass through as values for the caller. Both functions are `@ total`, and the client sees only the interfaces.

stops.title: A rejected client
stops.text: This client claims that every complete request has an empty body. The laws do not imply it, since a request with a Content-Length has a body, and the checker reports a counterexample at `()`, pointing at the claimed refinement; the test compiles the client against the grammar and parser interfaces plus the pure model. `http_suffix_rejected.ml` fails to prove that parsing discards a pipelined suffix, and `http_private_rejected.ml` cannot name `Vox_http.Internal`. `http_rejection_rejected.ml` checks seven false claims about the line-error laws, for example that an invalid request line is reported as `Invalid_header`.

stops.title: The invariant behind the abstract state
stops.text: The public `state` refines the machine state by `good`: the budget is in range, `valid_core` holds (the lines absorbed so far are valid, and a body is within its framed length), and, unless the core is an error, the bytes it has absorbed (`core_wire`) are exactly as many as the budget spent. `good` is stated of `Driver.model machine`, the machine with its lists put back in order, because the executable parser keeps them reversed. `state` is abstract in the interface, so every state a client holds was built by `initial` or `feed`, which prove `good`, and `state_sound` follows from it. `status` maps the `Line` and `Body` cores to `Incomplete` and passes terminal cores through.

stops.title: The core proof: completeness
stops.text: Completeness is proved on the machine in three steps. `serializer_core_roundtrip` shows that draining the serialization of a `well_formed` request from the initial core ends in `Complete request` with no input left; `feed_matches_drain` shows that `feed` agrees with the budget-free `drain` on input that fits the budget; and `chunking_invariance` splits the input after the serialization, so the suffix meets a terminal state and comes back untouched. `chunking_invariance`, above, is an induction on the first chunk. The public law `roundtrip` restates this lemma through `Driver.model` and the observations.

stops.title: The parser that runs
stops.text: The executable parser is `Driver.consume`, a copy of the machine that keeps the current line, the header lines and the body as reversed lists, so each byte costs one cons, and `Driver.simulation` proves by induction that it computes `Model.feed` up to `Driver.model`. `run` calls it and discharges the public contract with `driver_result_facts` in erased code; `feed` is `run`. The demo trusts nothing beyond the base shared by all demos; the built-in meaning it relies on most is that `Vox_sequence.length` is the length of a list. Input is an OCaml list of integers, one per byte, and no cost theorem is stated.

stops.title: Streaming across chunk boundaries
stops.text: This example feeds two pipelined requests in six chunks, split inside a CRLF, inside a header name and inside the body. After each complete request `deliver` restarts from `initial ()` on the returned rest, which the contract makes safe: the rest is exactly the input after the request. `http_stream_demo.ml` runs it and compares its output with a reference. `http_parser.ml` runs the runtime tests: every two-chunk split of a pipeline, byte-at-a-time input, malformed lines, framing errors, the exact message and body limits, and the budget running out inside a header line and in the body. An empty chunk does not mean end of input, so a caller whose input ends in an `Incomplete` state must report truncation itself.
